sentences.text: Heard learned APP Mr. K. L. Pandya for the appellant - State R/CR.A/1336/2012 JUDGMENT and learned advocate Mr. Kartik I. Soni for the respondent.

2. The appellant - State has filed this appeal praying to enhance the sentence awarded to the respondent by the JMFC of Sagbara, District: Narmada in Criminal Case No. 543 of 2010 whereby respondent is convicted under Rule 32(C)(f)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and under Sections 2(9)(k) as well as 7(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

By such impugned judgment dated 27.02.2012, for above conviction the trial Court has awarded sentence in the form of simple imprisonment for 6 months and fine of Rs.100/- with condition that in default of payment of fine, respondent has to undergo simple imprisonment for further 15 days.

3. The case of the complainant, being Senior Food Inspector before the trial Court was to the effect that respondent herein is running a shop in the name and style of Saurashtra Cold-drinks and dealing with cold beverages like lemon, orange, rimzim, masal soda, kalakhatta, mango etc. and on the date of raid i.e. on 04.03.2004 the complainant has purchased 6 bottles of orange sweetened carbonated water after making payment and taken specimen from such bottles and on analysis, it was found that it was mis-branded and thereby complaint was lodged against respondent and after trial, he was convicted as aforesaid.

It is material to note that even while collecting the samples,
complainant has to disclose that he has purchased the material of Rimzim brand and, therefore, it becomes clear that respondent has not manufactured all such product, which is sold in a packed bottle and ready to serve.

It is also clear that even public analyst has after examination, simply reported that it is mis - branded but there is no result or report regarding any contents or adulteration or either R/CR.A/1336/2012 JUDGMENT presence of any material, which may be harmful to the human being or there is no proof regarding absence of any required ingredients or presence of any unwanted ingredients.
Thereby as per the report by the Public Analyst when the product is as per the standard laid down in the Act.

Practically, for mis-branding of the product,
there must be a complaint by the original manufacturer of particular brand.

Whereas so far as non-compliance of Section 2(9)
(k) of the Act is concerned, it is practically regarding improper label and not for adulteration and to that extent through it is an offence but it is not that kind of serious offence, for which conviction,
which is imposed by the trial Court, may be modified only because appeal is preferred.
4. Therefore, only allegation against the appellant is to the effect that he has failed to disclose that when the commodity is manufactured or packed.
The month and year and to be used best before the date are to be disclosed on label.

However, if we peruse the provisions of Rule 32(C)(f)(i) of the Rules, there is a proviso to such rule which makes it clear that though date, month or year of manufacture, pack or pre-pack are to be disclosed on label, it is mandatory only when commodity has short life of less than 3 months.

Though disclosure of such details is necessary as per the Act and Rules, only for non - disclosure of such fact, practically, there is no reason to interfere in the State Of Gujarat vs Gulam Mohmmed Tarmohmmed ... on 22 July, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29494383/
2 impugned judgment, which is otherwise a discretionary order.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, in addition to merits, learned advocate Mr. Soni has pointed out one another glaring fact that though impugned judgment and order is dated 27.02.2012 and though the appeal is filed only on 22.08.2012, the appellant has failed to disclose the filing of appeal by the respondent before the Sessions Court, R/CR.A/1336/2012 JUDGMENT Rajpipla against the same impugned judgment under Section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure being Criminal Appeal No. 3 of 2012 whereby Sessions Court has though confirmed the conviction, extended the benefit of Probation of Offenders'
Act to the respondent after following due procedure of law in the form of calling the report of Probation Officer, as requested by the respondent by an application at exhibit 13 of such appeal.

Therefore, it is contended by learned advocate for the respondent that though State has appeared in such appeal before the Sessions Court through public prosecutor and though report of Probation Officer was produced before the Sessions Court and though Sessions Court has decided the appeal on 26.06.212, while preferring this appeal on 22.08.2012 i.e. two months after the judgment by the Sessions Court, appellant herein has suppressed such facts and appeal was filed with an application to condone the delay which was allowed in absence of such information.

Learned advocate Mr.Soni has shown the certified copy of such judgment dated 26.06.2012 by the Sessions Court, Rajpipla in Criminal Appeal No. 3 of 2012, which is certainly against impugned order dated 22.02.2012 in Criminal Case No. 543 of 2010 by the JMFC, Sagbara.

6. Therefore, when the Sessions Court has already extended the benefit of probation, when there is suppression of material fact as well as when there is no substance in the appeal on its own merits also, I do not see any reason to interfere in the impugned judgment only for enhancement of the sentence, as prayed for, and, therefore, appeal deserves to be dismissed and hence, the same is hereby dismissed.
R & P, if any, called for be sent back to the concerned trial Court, forthwith.
R/CR.A/1336/2012 JUDGMENT

(S.G.SHAH, J.)
